# 🧩 dsh-moa-native
**Native Mixture-of-Agents for DeepSeek Harness — generation-time fusion**: reference models produce
pre-run drafts in parallel every turn; the single acting model executes with full tooling.
English | 中文说明
## What it solves
A single model has blind spots. In long sessions you want a few models reviewing the situation behin
d every reply — without switching tools, copy-pasting, or giving up tool use. dsh-moa-native interna
lizes that loop: **picking one model entry runs the whole MoA pipeline for the session**.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Recommended mode (advanced)
**F mirror + 3-4 heterogeneous blank-injection refs + a single aggregator + the parallel-plan discip
line** — one glance:
- Every ref uses the `__blank__` injection (zero instruction, pure continuation — pure model-family

signal, no persona noise);
- The aggregator uses `agg_forrefsblank` (candidate action plans: where a
draft agrees with your own judgement it is worth more weight, disagreements are judged independentl

y, all actions executed by the aggregator itself);
- The factory `default` stays Hermes-aligned (rev
iew-style refs with the default injection) — start there, switch to the recommended combo once famil
style refs with the default injection) — start there, switch to the recommended combo once familiar.
Full part-by-part, parameter-by-parameter walkthrough: architecture.svg.
## Tiered rhythm (v4.4.0)
**Heavy models steer every *m* steps, flash models patrol every *n* steps, and every other step reus
es the last beat — free while that beat is still cached (a cache miss refills with the patrol roster
he last beat — free while that beat is still cached (a cache miss refills with the patrol roster).**
- **Cadence is the fourth tier** — `user_turn` (once per user turn, cheapest), `per_iteration` (ever
y step), `every_n×N` (skip N steps after each fan-out, so the period is N+1 steps), and `tiered` (th

e rhythm below);
- **Two roles, two periods**: the *steering* beat asks heavy models (`@max` / `@xhi
gh`) whether the direction is still right — every *m* steps; the *patrol* beat asks flash refs wheth

er the execution has drifted — every *n* steps;
- **Non-beat steps are frozen**: the previous beat's

guidance is reused verbatim, at zero ref cost;
- **One beat, one job**: when a step is due for both

, steering wins and the patrol beat is suppressed;
- **Where the rosters live**: `cadence_tiered.ste
ering` (the heavy models) and `cadence_tiered.patrol` (the flash models — omit it to keep patrol fol

lowing `refs`); under the tiered cadence a recipe's own `refs` are just the patrol fallback pool;
-
**The model never sees the rhythm itself**: beat vocabulary, failures and scale stay host-side (trac
e + console only) — the injected text carries no beat words, no failure notices and no counts (block
*count* remains a first-order proxy, as the design doc states honestly).

## Quick start
1. Settings → **MoA-Native console**: pick 3-4 reference routes (flash tiers work well — fast and ch
eap) and one aggregator (the model you want to keep). **This step is mandatory on first install** —
the factory lineup is only an example and must point at your own configured providers/models. Since
references are framed as the aggregator's own pre-run drafts, you can skip a ref that shares the agg

regator's model (saves one route).
2. Save (hot-reloads), then select a **moa-native** entry in the

session model picker — `default` or any recipe you saved.
3. Chat normally. Fusion happens every tur
n; `/moaR` `/moaF` temporarily switch the **reference view** (lineup, aggregator, and cadence stay w
ith the current entry; the console shows the live *slash preview*). Subagent sessions stream straigh
t through the aggregator by default (zero fanout) — switch via the *subagent gating* dropdown (7 tie
## Highlights
**Config as model** — `default` and every recipe appear as model entries on the provider page; a rec
ipe is a full preset (lineup, mode, cadence, params).
**Three-level model picker** (identical to the session UI) — provider → model → effort for every rou
hree-level model picker** (identical to the session UI) — provider → model → effort for every route.
**Injection modules** — each route's trailing note is a visible, editable text module: built-in defa
ult (Hermes-style), blank (zero injection), or any custom one. No hidden personas, no output-length
s-style), blank (zero injection), or any custom one. No hidden personas, no output-length contracts.
**Two reference modes** — the default is **F**; pick R when the input bill matters more than perfect

fidelity:
- **F · full mirror** *(default)* — references see exactly what the acting model sees; KV
prefix cache hit rates above 90%. **Costs the most**: every reference route bills the full system +
tools + history on every beat, so the input spend scales with conversation length. The recommended
lineup (F + blank-injection flash refs + tiered cadence + anchored guidance) exists precisely to kee
p this bill low — flash-tier refs, frozen reuse between beats, −36% uncached tokens vs the trailing

form.
- **R · trimmed view** — Hermes-style tool-result trimming; drops the system prompt, folds too
l results. The economy lane. Its overall window is **per-model dynamic** (4.5.2): each route's budge
t comes from its own registered context window — `(window × 0.9 − 8192) × 1.5` chars, the whole flee
t flying on the minimum, so a 64k ref tightens the view and a 1M ref sees more. Tool results truncat
e at Hermes' own 4,000 chars (`ref_tool_result_budget`); `ref_input_char_budget`, when set, caps the
dynamic budget. Unknown windows ride the conservative 128k baseline (warned once; fill `contextWind
ow` in `DSH-MoA-model-registry.json` to enable exact adaptation).
**Subagent gating** — MoA applies to the main session by default; subagent sessions pass straight th
rough the aggregator, with an optional every-N-steps upgrade. Design rationale: SUBAGENT-GATING-DESI
the aggregator, with an optional every-N-steps upgrade. Design rationale: SUBAGENT-GATING-DESIGN.md.
